labels.title: Yellow Emperor's Inner Canon
labels.description: The foundational classic of Chinese medicine

chapters.summary: Discusses how ancient people understood health preservation

sections.title: Ancient Heaven and Truth Chapter One
sections.originalText: 昔在黄帝，生而神灵，弱而能言，幼而徇齐，长而敦敏，成而聪明。上问于天师曰：余闻上古之人，春秋皆度百岁，而动作不衰；今时之人，年半百而动作皆衰者，时世异耶？人将失之耶？岐伯对曰：上古之人，其知道者，法于阴阳，和于术数，食饮有节，起居有常，不妄作劳，故能形与神俱，而尽终其天年。
sections.translation: In ancient times, the Yellow Emperor was born divine, able to speak in infancy, precocious in childhood, earnest and diligent in youth, and intelligent in adulthood. He asked his heavenly master: I have heard that ancient people all lived beyond 100 years without decline in their activities; now people at 50 have declining abilities. Is it due to different times, or have people lost something? Qi Bo answered: Ancient people who understood the Way followed yin and yang, harmonized with methods, had regulated diet and drink, regular routine, did not overwork, thus could maintain both form and spirit to complete their natural lifespan.
sections.interpretation: This passage expounds the core concept of health preservation in Chinese medicine. It reflects the holistic concept of unity of heaven and humanity, emphasizing that humans should follow natural laws and maintain yin-yang balance for health and longevity.

keyConcepts.description: The core concept of Chinese philosophy, referring to the two fundamental forces in the universe that are opposite yet interdependent
The philosophical concept that humans are an integral part of nature and should follow natural laws

title.en: On the Four Qi to Adjust the Spirit

chapters.summary: Discusses how to maintain health by adapting to the four seasons' qi changes

sections.title: Four Qi Spirit Regulation Chapter One
sections.originalText: 春三月，此谓发陈。天地俱生，万物以荣。夜卧早起，广步于庭，被发缓形，以使志生。生而勿杀，予而勿夺，赏而勿罚。此春气之应，养生之道也。
sections.translation: The three months of spring are called development and blooming. Heaven and earth both give birth, and all things flourish. Sleep late at night and rise early, walk widely in the courtyard, loosen hair and relax body, to enable the will to arise. Give birth but do not kill, give but do not take away, reward but do not punish. This is responding to spring qi, the way of health preservation.
sections.interpretation: This chapter describes the health preservation principles for spring. Spring is the season of growth and development, corresponding to wood element and liver in Chinese medicine.

keyConcepts.description: Health preservation methods by adapting to seasonal qi changes
The qi characteristics of spring season, corresponding to growth and development

keyPoints: Established the theoretical foundation of Chinese medicine
Systematically expounded yin-yang and five elements theory
Created the zang-fu organ and meridian theory
clinicalApplications: Guiding principles for diagnosis and treatment
Foundation for acupuncture and moxibustion theory
historicalSignificance: Influenced medical development for over 2000 years
Foundation of all Chinese medicine schools
Cultural treasure of world medical history
